courses.title: Lesson 1 | Where do first-time global startups most often fail?
courses.desc: Identify common misconceptions in global entrepreneurship, distinguish transferable domestic-market experience from assumptions that can lead teams astray, and understand the early pitfalls of entering international markets.

courses.title: Lesson 2 | What makes a growth strategy effective?
courses.desc: Look beyond impressions, followers, rankings, and sign-ups. Evaluate growth work through target users, product onboarding, activation, retention, payment, and repeatability.

courses.title: Lesson 3 | The global growth process and team setup
courses.desc: Learn the right sequence for early-stage global growth and how user research, value proposition, competitors, website, launch, and retrospectives fit together—plus how a small team can get started.

courses.title: Lesson 4 | Competitor research: the answer to your hardest question may already exist
courses.desc: Analyze competitor websites, past versions, social channels, and launch cadence to find positioning and growth insights in the paths they have already taken.

courses.title: Lesson 5 | How do you define a value proposition the world can understand?
courses.desc: Turn complex product capabilities into a message target users can grasp quickly, then apply it to your website hero, outreach, and product introduction.

courses.title: Lesson 6 | How do you find your first 10 users worldwide?
courses.desc: Find early users, build a target list, design personalized outreach at scale, and identify potential core users through real replies.

courses.title: Lesson 7 | How do you run effective user interviews?
courses.desc: Design an interview process that uncovers real workflows, reasons to switch, buying signals, and priorities for product improvement.

courses.title: Lesson 8 | How do you validate PMF?
courses.desc: Use evidence from retention, payment, repeat purchases, and referrals to judge product-market fit—and decide whether to keep refining or scale up.

courses.title: Lesson 9 | SEO / GEO growth methodology
courses.desc: Help your product appear consistently in search engines and AI answers. Understand keywords, structured content, long-tail coverage, and the full path from visibility to conversion.

courses.title: Lesson 10 | How do you build a high-converting website?
courses.desc: Use the first three screens of your website to help users understand the product, decide if it fits, build trust, and take action.

courses.title: Lesson 11 | GitHub open-source operations
courses.desc: Turn GitHub from a code repository into a developer growth channel, with a systematic operating plan before, during, and after launch.

courses.title: Lesson 12 | The complete Product Hunt launch guide
courses.desc: Decide when your product is ready, then prepare, coordinate, support, and review Product Hunt as a 24-hour global launch campaign.

courses.title: Lesson 13 | YouTube operations
courses.desc: Decide when to build a channel, test ads, or work with creators—and identify conversion signals that matter beyond view counts.

courses.title: Lesson 14 | X operations
courses.desc: Use content, DMs, APIs, and tools for scaled outreach while keeping operations manageable across efficiency, account safety, and genuine conversion.

courses.title: Lesson 15 | Reddit operations
courses.desc: Understand Reddit's community rules and language, then build a reviewable community program through user research, credible content, and lasting search assets.

courses.title: Lesson 16 | LinkedIn operations
courses.desc: For B2B, SMB, and prosumer products, use content, targeted campaigns, DMs, and events to turn professional relationships into sales leads.

courses.title: Lesson 17 | TikTok operations
courses.desc: Assess whether TikTok fits your product, understand when to use short-form video, account portfolios, and ads, and measure channel value through activation, payment, and repeat purchases.

courses.title: Lesson 18 | Product community operations
courses.desc: Bring scattered users together through communities, events, referrals, and sales leads, building localized growth infrastructure that supports sales, channels, and customer success.

courses.title: Special Topic 1 | How do you build a cross-border team?
courses.desc: Decide when a local team is truly needed and how to progress from market validation, community pilots, and channel tests to a cross-border organization.

courses.title: Special Topic 2 | How do you expand overseas after years in the domestic market?
courses.desc: Identify which domestic-market experience transfers, what needs adjustment, and what must be rebuilt—without using the domestic market as a map for overseas customers.

courses.title: Special Topic 3 | How do you expand overseas compliantly?
courses.desc: Understand stage-specific risks in data, privacy, contracts, certification, and cross-border operations; decide when third-party services are enough and when to seek legal counsel.
